title: What The Bagpipes Know — EN/GA/DE (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 98bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal Scottish Gaelic German Celtic philosophy language learning
lyrics:
[Verse 1 — English]
The bagpipes were weaponised at the Battle of Waterloo
A piper led the troops in because someone felt it's what you do
The English banned the bagpipes for a time as an instrument of war
Which tells you something about what the bagpipes are for

[Verse 2 — Scottish Gaelic, with English translation]
Tha na pìoban-mòra a' toirt cliù do Alba
[The great pipes bring glory to Scotland]
Cluinnear iad air gach cnoc, ann an gach gleann
[They are heard on every hill, in every glen]
Tha fàileadh na mòna anns gach port
[There is the scent of peat in every tune]
Na pìoban-mòra — innsidh iad ar sgeulachd
[The great pipes — they tell our story]

[Chorus — English]
What do the bagpipes know that I don't know?
They know that every funeral gets better with the drone below
What do the bagpipes know on a Scottish hill?
They know the sound of grief and joy are both the same until
That's my boy

[Bridge — German, with English translation]
Die Dudelsäcke klingen wie der Wind durch die Highlands
[The bagpipes sound like wind through the Highlands]
Ein altes Instrument für alte, harte Lands
[An ancient instrument for ancient, hard lands]
Die Deutschen haben auch Sackpfeifen, die wenige kennen
[The Germans also have bagpipes that few know about]
Aber Schottlands Pfeifen — die kann man nicht vergessen
[But Scotland's pipes — those cannot be forgotten]

[Outro — All three languages]
What the bagpipes know… Dè tha fios aig na pìoban… Was der Dudelsack weiß
Older than the argument — Nas sine na an còmhstri — Älter als der Streit
That's my boy
